newsitem.title: INDIA: India call at 0.1-0.5 pct, RBI revises sale prices.
newsitem.headline: India call at 0.1-0.5 pct, RBI revises sale prices.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted at 0 0.1-0.5 percent in early Friday trade with few deals struck, dealers said.
They said there were more lenders than borrowers in the market.
"At the moment, it is mainly quotes," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "There are very few borrowers and in fact lenders are wondering whom to lend to."
Dealers said they expected the gilts market to remain active on Friday. Gilt prices have been on the upswing in the last few days on low call money rates and expectations of a fall in interest rates.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) revised sale prices upwards in its price-list for open market operations effective April 4.

The RBI has hiked its selling price of the 11.64 percent 2000 stock to 97.78 rupees from 97.32, the 11.00 percent 2002 to 93.53 from 93.04, the 11.00 percent 2003 to 92.07 from 91.60, the 7.00 percent 2009 to 62.18 from 62.04 and the 8.75 percent 2010 to 71.11 from 70.96.
